resultText:
This looks correct.

## Root cause

`isUniqueItem` in `packages/excalidraw/data/library.ts` treated two library items as "the same" only if every element matched by both `id` **and** `versionNonce`, in order. But `versionNonce` isn't stable across imports: `restoreElements` runs `syncInvalidIndices` on freshly-loaded items, and whenever an element's fractional `index` needs fixing (which happens essentially every time a library is loaded from a file/URL, since serialized elements rarely carry indices valid within the freshly-restored array), `mutateElement` regenerates a random `versionNonce` (`packages/element/src/mutateElement.ts:140`) as a side effect of that unrelated update. So re-importing the exact same library file produces elements with the same `id`s but a brand-new random `versionNonce` every time, causing the dedup check to always fail and duplicate every item.

## Fix

Dropped the `versionNonce` comparison and dedupe purely on element `id`s (still compared positionally, index by index):
- Same ids in the same order at the same count → treated as duplicate → nothing added on re-import.
- Same elements in a different order, or a different element count → still treated as different (length/order checks preserved).
- Genuinely new/different items (different ids) → still added.

No test runner is available in this environment, so I wasn't able to execute `yarn test:update`/`yarn test:typecheck` — worth running those before committing.
